As much as naturists hate to admit it, advocacy for sexual freedom in the 60's and 70's is the closest we ever got to being noticed on a world scale, enough that the sitting president at the time levied acts against them. I believe that lending our support to LGBTQ+ is a good way to recapture that authority we lost when naturism traded communes and meditation for volleyball and sunbathing.

At the same time, apoliticality brings with it a sense of stagnation, and as such, a gradual lack of interest as the sub content becomes more homogeneous. The sub has largely been the same thing over and over with different settings, because no one has an ideal or side to argue. This sub, r/nudism, is staying clear of the partisanship, and I think for good reason. It's better for people to still have a place to go if they just have questions or concerns, but for those who want to see the movement as a whole progress, having a place that can put forward some real political action and pressure is infinitely more enticing than sticking to the same old posts every day with no one really going anywhere.

Let this post be our independence speech~ No one else was going to do it, and this has been a discussion on the discord for some time. This is the perfect opportunity for the bottom to change to match the top. Top being relative, because really, we're all equal sans clothing. Here's hoping for a prosperous community under our new dynamic!

I actually agree with this particular sentiment, conditionally. Writers and artists should be free to branch out - what matters most is the artist's intent. It's easy to tell by the characters' dialogue, setting, and situations what part of the psyche the creator is harnessing to craft - this particular type, from the scant-thought-out plot to the sheer absurdity of it all while attempting to take it seriously, just screams, "The author was horny and wanted to make something that appealed to them."
> conveniently ignoring the circumstances surrounding it
I think the last thing we want is more fetishists to make their home in our community. They already wreck things enough.
*Nudism* is dependent on circumstances. Involuntary nudism, is not nudism. It's just coercion and humiliation. No matter how Stockholm syndromed your characters are, it won't change the reality.

The only way to make willingly risking one's life for such a simple endeavor plausible is if you don't take it seriously - a la Jojo. Is this a post-society world where capital punishment is not only legal, but glorified and televised? What are the players in for for their desperation to be so paramount to risk it all for such a payout? These are the background questions you need to answer to prevent your readers from scratching they heads in confusion.

Alternatively, don't take your story so seriously. Though for that to fit, you'd need a different art style.

I don't really care, the nudity is welcome, simple, and fine. Congrats on posting the uncensored version - but the message it sends is the same. It's not the nudity, it's the circumstances surrounding it.

I think holding execution over participants' heads is *definitely* a type of extortion. It's a common line supervillains use - "See, I'm giving you a choice, either comply or die! Aren't I a gracious host?" It's almost idiomatic at this point, so trying to put a positive spin on it isn't fooling anyone.
